# `js/max-params`

**A function takes at most a maximum number of parameters**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:js/size` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `max`, `count_this`, `count_varargs`, `ignore_names`, `ignore_overrides`, `ignore_declarations`, `ignore_constructor_injection` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (grouping parameters changes the function's signature and every call to it; which belong together is the author's call) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint/max-params`, `typescript-eslint/max-params` |

## What it checks

A function takes at most `max` parameters (3 by default). A destructured object or array parameter counts as one, which
is the usual way out. A rest parameter and a TypeScript `this:` parameter are not counted unless `count_varargs` or
`count_this` is `true`, and neither is a parameter whose name matches `ignore_names` (`"^_"` by default: a
parameter named `_unused` is already said to be unused). A TypeScript `override` method, an overload signature, a
`declare` function, an abstract method and anything in a `.d.ts` file are skipped, since you do not own that
signature; set `ignore_overrides` or `ignore_declarations` to `false` to count them. A constructor that only
declares parameter properties (`constructor(private a: A, private b: B)`) can be skipped with
`ignore_constructor_injection`. The rule reports on the function's name: `createOrder takes 6 parameters (max 3)`.

**Why:** A call with many positional arguments is easy to get in the wrong order, and every added parameter is a change to every
caller. Grouping related parameters in one object names them at the call site.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:js/size` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/size"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/max-params" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `integer` | `3` | the most parameters a function may take |
| `count_this` | `boolean` | `false` | TypeScript: count a `this:` parameter |
| `count_varargs` | `boolean` | `false` | count a rest parameter, `...rest` |
| `ignore_names` | `string` | `"^_"` | a regular expression; parameters named like this do not count |
| `ignore_overrides` | `boolean` | `true` | skip a TypeScript `override` method: its signature is not yours |
| `ignore_declarations` | `boolean` | `true` | skip an overload signature, a `declare` function, an abstract method and a `.d.ts` file |
| `ignore_constructor_injection` | `boolean` | `false` | TypeScript: skip a constructor whose parameters are all parameter properties (Angular, NestJS) |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/max-params"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 3
count_this = false
count_varargs = false
ignore_names = "^_"
ignore_overrides = true
ignore_declarations = true
ignore_constructor_injection = false
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/max-params" = { severity = "error", options = { max = 2, count_this = true, count_varargs = true, ignore_names = "^_", ignore_overrides = false, ignore_declarations = false, ignore_constructor_injection = true } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `max`

*integer* · default `3`

the most parameters a function may take

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

#### `count_this`

*boolean* · default `false`

TypeScript: count a `this:` parameter

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
count_this = true
```

#### `count_varargs`

*boolean* · default `false`

count a rest parameter, `...rest`

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
count_varargs = true
```

#### `ignore_names`

*string* · default `"^_"`

a regular expression; parameters named like this do not count

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
ignore_names = "^_"
```

#### `ignore_overrides`

*boolean* · default `true`

skip a TypeScript `override` method: its signature is not yours

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
ignore_overrides = false
```

#### `ignore_declarations`

*boolean* · default `true`

skip an overload signature, a `declare` function, an abstract method and a `.d.ts` file

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
ignore_declarations = false
```

#### `ignore_constructor_injection`

*boolean* · default `false`

TypeScript: skip a constructor whose parameters are all parameter properties (Angular, NestJS)

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
ignore_constructor_injection = true
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/max-params.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a function declaration

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
function a(x, y, z) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:10`.

#### an arrow function

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
const f = (x, y, z) => 1;
```

**Reports** at `1:7`.

#### a single arrow parameter without parentheses

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 0
```

```js
const f = x => x;
```

**Reports** at `1:7`.

#### a method and a constructor

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
class A {
  constructor(a, b, c) {}
  run(a, b, c) {}
}
```

**Reports** at `2:3`, `3:3`.

#### a generator and an async function

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
function* g(a, b, c) {}
async function f(a, b, c) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:11`, `2:16`.

#### a destructured parameter is one

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
function a({ x, y, z }, [b, c]) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### default values count

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
function a(x, y = 1, z = 2) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:10`.

#### a rest parameter is not counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
function a(x, y, ...rest) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a rest parameter, counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
count_varargs = true
```

```js
function a(x, y, ...rest) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:10`.

#### ignore_names

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_names = "^_"
```

```js
function a(x, _y, _z) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a parameter that does not match ignore_names is counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_names = "^_"
```

```js
function a(x, y, z, _w) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:10`.

#### a function at the limit passes

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```js
function a(x, y) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a TypeScript this parameter is not counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```ts
function a(this: Foo, x: number, y: number) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a TypeScript this parameter, counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
count_this = true
```

```ts
function a(this: Foo, x: number, y: number) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:10`.

#### a TypeScript override method is skipped

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```ts
class A extends B {
  override run(a: number, b: number, c: number) {}
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a TypeScript override method, counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_overrides = false
```

```ts
class A extends B {
  override run(a: number, b: number, c: number) {}
}
```

**Reports** at `2:12`.

#### a TypeScript overload signature and a declare function are skipped

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```ts
declare function a(x: number, y: number, z: number): void;
function b(x: number, y: number, z: number): void;
function b(x: any, y: any, z: any) {}
```

**Reports** at `3:10`.

#### a TypeScript abstract method is skipped

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```ts
abstract class A {
  abstract run(a: number, b: number, c: number): void;
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### declarations, counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_declarations = false
```

```ts
declare function a(x: number, y: number, z: number): void;
abstract class A {
  abstract run(a: number, b: number, c: number): void;
}
```

**Reports** at `1:18`, `3:12`.

#### constructor injection

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```ts
class A {
  constructor(private a: X, private b: Y, readonly c: Z) {}
}
```

**Reports** at `2:3`.

#### constructor injection, skipped

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_constructor_injection = true
```

```ts
class A {
  constructor(private a: X, private b: Y, readonly c: Z) {}
}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### constructor injection mixed with a plain parameter is counted

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_constructor_injection = true
```

```ts
class A {
  constructor(private a: X, private b: Y, c: Z) {}
}
```

**Reports** at `2:3`.

#### a TSX component

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
```

```tsx
const A = (a: number, b: number, c: number) => <i />;
```

**Reports** at `1:7`.

#### an invalid ignore_names is reported once, and the function still measured

```toml
[rules."js/max-params".options]
max = 2
ignore_names = "("
```

```js
function a(x, y, z) {}
```

**Reports** at `1:1`, `1:10`.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/max-params" = { options = { max = 2 } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/max-params" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/max-params" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/max-params" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/max-params" = { severity = "warn", options = { max = 2 } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/max-params": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"max": 2}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/max-params: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/max-params expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/max-params --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/max-params        # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/max-params   # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>  # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Group the parameters that belong together into one options object: `createOrder({ customer, items, coupon, address })`.
2. Update the callers to pass the object, and give the destructured parameter a type in TypeScript.
3. If the signature is not yours to change, exempt it: an `override`, an overload and a `declare` function already are.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
function createOrder(customer, items, coupon, address) {
  return { customer, items, coupon, address };
}
```

#### Do

```js
function createOrder({ customer, items, coupon, address }) {
  return { customer, items, coupon, address };
}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
function Card(title, body, footer, onClose) {
  return <div>{title}{body}{footer}{onClose}</div>;
}
```

#### Do

```jsx
function Card({ title, body, footer, onClose }) {
  return <div>{title}{body}{footer}{onClose}</div>;
}
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
function createOrder(customer: string, items: string[], coupon: string, address: string) {
  return { customer, items, coupon, address };
}
```

#### Do

```ts
function createOrder({ customer, items, coupon, address }: Order) {
  return { customer, items, coupon, address };
}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
function Card(title: string, body: string, footer: string, onClose: () => void) {
  return <div>{title}{body}{footer}{onClose}</div>;
}
```

#### Do

```tsx
function Card({ title, body, footer, onClose }: CardProps) {
  return <div>{title}{body}{footer}{onClose}</div>;
}
```
